what: Round 1310 (league book Round F, a data job). The real yardstick for Club Manager's league leaders: the league goals of each league's leading scorer for 2015-16 to 2024-25 in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, the Bundesliga and Ligue 1, each with the league matches a club played that season, and the leading keeper's league clean sheets wherever two publishers could be opened. Read by a harness only (scripts/simCmLeagueBook.mjs, section facts, Round 1311). No page, no bundle and no file under src reads it: scripts/simCmLeagueBookFacts.mjs holds that.
rules: A ROW is one opened page read for one season (or, for a format row, the span of seasons the page speaks for). Every literal is a line the page reader quoted from that page; a table row is its cells in order with single spaces between them. A figure is a number printed in one of its row's literals.

A FIGURE is one quantity in one competition in one season. It is USED only when two independent publishers on two different hosts each print it in a quoted literal AND AGREE EXACTLY. One publisher is THIN, however many seasons it lists. Two that differ are DISPUTED: both rows stay on file, nothing is averaged and nothing is picked by preference. scripts/simCmLeagueBookFacts.mjs works the three states out from the rows alone; no field here types one.

WHAT A COUNT IS: each row's counts says whose count it is (a league's own list, a newspaper's award, an archive). A league's count and a paper's that differ are DISPUTED, never settled by choosing one.

THE MATCHES A CLUB PLAYED come from FORMAT rows only, never from a top scorer row: a span row is a publisher saying how many clubs the league had over a run of seasons, a season row is one season's final table. The length a format row gives is the matches it prints, or twice one less than the clubs it prints (a club plays every other club twice). The pandemic broke 2019-20 in every league (Ligue 1 stopped it; the other four paused it and played it out, which their season tables show with 38 or 34 played, while the pause itself is quoted only for the Bundesliga, see notUsed), so that season's length stands on season rows only: a span row says the league's size, not whether that season finished. A season stopped early is curtailed and belongs to no length.
Every core row (a topScorerGoals or keeperCleanSheets row) carries length, the matches a club played as the format rows give it, or curtailed.

THE CORE is topScorerGoals with its length, for all five leagues and all ten seasons. Every core cell is USED or named under owed with what was looked for. keeperCleanSheets is printed only and binds nothing; a keeper cell that is not USED is named under owed the same way.

SOURCES: every page opened with the page reader; never a search summary; never a wiki host (wikipedia, wikimedia, fandom, any host starting wiki.), never Transfermarkt or Futbin. The league's own site plus an independent archive or outlet first; a list page of an aggregator only as a second publisher when no outlet opened, and the receipt names it.

Literals are table lines and headings, and where a row needs a sentence (a league's own guide or FAQ on its size, an outlet's own narration in a report of the day, an archive's NB note under a table) the publisher's own words; never a person's words and never a line a page puts in a person's mouth. A page's en dash or em dash is written here as a hyphen.

owed.lookedFor: DISPUTED, so on file and unused. RSSSF's list of the Pichichi (rsssf.org/tabless/spantops.html, Marca's count) prints 37 for Karim Benzema, asked for twice digit by digit; 90min's list and ESPN's scoring table of the season each print 27. Nothing is picked by preference and no reading is dropped. It closes when the lead rules, or when a reading that settles whose count the 37 is (Marca's own palmares page, LaLiga's own season stats; neither opened to the page reader on 2026-10-12) is filed and every reading on file agrees.

THIN: no reading on file. La Liga gives no award for clean sheets (its Zamora goes to the best goals conceded a match), so no list by season exists the way the Golden Glove's does. Read on 2026-10-12: laliga.com's article on the five best goalkeepers of the 2024/25 league season (laliga.com's English news section, 19.07.2025; cited by host and date, since its address carries the league's sponsored name) prints goals conceded and matches, no clean sheets; squawka.com's La Liga clean sheets page answers 403; fbref.com answers 403. A search summary put Jan Oblak on 15 in 2024-25 and that is not a reading. Owed to the match engine round the critic's answer 7 names: two opened publishers a season, for example a season's stats page of a data outlet and a club's or a newspaper's season report.

THIN: no reading on file. Serie A gives no award for clean sheets, and no list by season was looked for in this round once La Liga's search showed what it costs (one page a season a publisher, with fbref.com, the one archive that lists them, answering 403). Owed to the match engine round, as La Liga's.

notUsed: Premier League keepers, a third list opened on 2026-10-12 and not filed as rows: https://www.mykhel.com/football/premier-league-golden-glove-winners-list-l8/ is headed as a golden boot list over a table titled for the World Cup, with a Matches column of noughts beside the clean sheets. Its clean sheet column agrees with both filed publishers on 2015-16 to 2021-22 and it has no row after that. Not filed: a page that mislabels its own table is no publisher's count of anything.

Premier League top scorers, a third list opened on 2026-10-12 and not filed as rows: https://footballberry.com/premier-league-golden-boot-winners-list/ (an aggregator's list page, Round 1229's second source) agrees with both filed publishers on all ten seasons. Two publishers make a figure USED; a third that agrees adds nothing the fence reads.

The pause of 2019-20 in the Premier League, La Liga and Serie A is not quoted by any row: RSSSF's season pages of those three carry no note on it (England's notes are for the divisions below), and no other page was opened for it. What binds is that each finished: two season tables each (RSSSF and ESPN) print 38 played. Only the Bundesliga's pause is quoted (RSSSF's note, league suspended for 10 weeks), and Ligue 1's stop twice (RSSSF and NBC Sports).
